body.statement: The family \(P^{\circ}\), indexed by \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), has an \((X,Z)\)-marginal density bounded and strictly positive on its finite rectangle support and uniformly bounded observed outcomes. It satisfies the marginal quasi-stayer part of Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024), while baseline-conditional positivity \(P(|Z|\le\eta\mid X)>0\) fails throughout \([-1,0)\), a baseline region of probability \(p_{\circ}\). The displayed laws \(Q_+^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}\) share \(P^{\circ}\), satisfy the source's Assumptions 1--4, including parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support, and in fact satisfy the stronger all-\(I\) equality because their period difference is dose-invariant. They have different WAOSS values. Therefore the Appendix step immediately before display (4) does not follow from the proceedings paper's marginal Assumption 4.
body.justification: A regular region, rather than a hand-tuned atom, establishes that the support defect has substantive identifying consequences.
body.gap: Theorem 1 of the proceedings paper states identification under Assumptions 1--4, but Assumption 4 is marginal and its Appendix proof invokes stronger baseline-conditional positivity immediately before display (4). The explicit conditional support regime in arXiv:2201.06898v1 handles the point-identified case, not the full-law sharp set on the positive-mass failure region exhibited here.
body.consumer: Users of the published WAOSS estimator obtain an exact support diagnostic identifying when its nonparametric formula remains justified.
